source.quote:
Notes — Normally the 6th house is treated as Dusthana (bad house); but if the lord of the sixth be in the sixth, he improves the effects of the 6th house. It is generally said by the astrological pandits that malefics do good if they are posited

<!-- page phaladeepika/p0077 -->
in the 6th house. The reason for this can be that the 6th house is 'Shatru sthana'. Malefics will destroy the enemies. It is also believed that Mars, Saturn and Rahu are good in the 3rd, 6th and 11th. The reason for this is also the same, namely, the malefic will destroy enemies and diseases. Now we come to Shri Mantreshwarar's views. According to him the lord of a house gives good effects when he is vested with strength. This is unobjectionable but he has also expressed the opinion that if lord of a Dusthana is posited in another dustnana he does good. This has been described in Verse 57 of this very chapter. Another thing is that benefics do good to the house where they are posited. Similarly the aspect of benefics improves the effects of the aspected house.

cards.note: Mantreswara's own primary Kemadruma definition (v. 5): the yoga is present when 'the above three Yogas' -- Sunapha, Anapha and Durudhara -- are absent, and those three collectively require a planet in the 2nd or 12th house from the Moon (dep.graha-frame); Kemadruma therefore fires when no such planet exists. 'Planets' is read as any graha the engine tracks other than the Moon itself (Sun, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu), because the verse states no exclusion -- contrast Hora Sara's variant (Notes, p.58), which explicitly excludes the Sun and nodes from nullifying the yoga; that exclusion is not imported here. Three further competing definitions in the same passage are recorded separately rather than merged into this condition: the verse's own hedged aside ('some learned are of the opinion'), Saravali's version and Hora Sara's version (both Notes), and five more attributed to Jataka Parijata, of which item (1) is independently testable and encoded separately as PD.06.Kemadruma.JatakaParijata1.
